critic_evaluation.feedback: The no-change decision is technically coherent with the visible target of 26 hours and preserves fixed workshops, sleep, and gym sessions. However, as a human-centered schedule, the calendar is only partially substantiated. The main concern is not that the events overlap, but that the preserved arrangement creates a very dense week with limited visible recovery: two 8-hour workdays around two full workshop days, followed by a 10-hour Friday work block after gym. The proposal should either provide a grounded reason why the existing Friday concentration is acceptable in the fuller context, or reconsider whether the same 26-hour target could be distributed in a way that reduces end-of-week load without undermining protected sleep, gym, and workshop commitments. This does not prove the calendar is impossible, and the issue may be pre-existing rather than introduced by the proposal, but choosing no changes still requires explaining why the visible burden is sustainable.

critic_evaluation.feedback: The revised schedule is more human-manageable than the prior no-change version because it removes the most visibly strenuous feature: the Friday 10:30-20:30 design block after gym. The resulting pattern is still a full week: Monday gym plus 9 hours of design work, two fixed workshop days, Thursday gym plus 9 hours of design work, and Friday gym plus 8 hours of design work. However, the burden is now distributed more evenly and Friday ends earlier at 18:30, which plausibly improves end-of-week recovery. The proposal also explicitly acknowledges missing information about meals, breaks, commute, workshop preparation, and tolerance for long creative days. The remaining concerns are real but not strong enough on the visible record to require another revision: there is no objective incompatibility, protected sleep remains intact, Tuesday and Wednesday are kept free of client work, and the prior concern has received a grounded response through an actual redistribution. The Proposer should still clean up the stale work-duration descriptions and, if fuller context is available, confirm that the longer Monday and Thursday workdays are preferable to the prior Friday concentration.

plausibility_review.reason: The prior material concern about the Friday 10-hour block has been addressed in a concrete way: Friday design work now runs 10:30-18:30 instead of 10:30-20:30, with the same 26 weekly work hours preserved. The new plan introduces two longer 9-hour workdays on Monday and Thursday, both after gym, and Thursday follows two workshop days, so cumulative fatigue remains a material uncertainty if the user has low tolerance for long creative workdays. Still, the visible evidence shows improvement rather than deterioration, and the remaining uncertainty is not enough by itself to require another revision because the calendar preserves sleep, fixed workshops, gym routines, and avoids client work on Tuesday and Wednesday. Another review could help only if fuller context reveals that 9-hour workdays after gym are not sustainable; otherwise the current trade-off is plausibly manageable.
plausibility_review.suggested_improvement: Keep the redistributed structure if it matches the fuller context, but correct the event-duration descriptions and verify whether Monday and Thursday 10:30-19:30 are genuinely preferable to a heavier Friday or another permitted distribution.
